pl-l4d45c6-d1e115.summary: Asks whether the saints hear the prayers of suppliants and whether petitioners' requests reach their knowledge.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e118.summary: Answers that it is not incredible that the saints' souls, rejoicing in the hidden face of God by the illumination of true light, understand in contemplating him what is done outside, as far as concerns their joy or our help; as to the angels, so to the saints who stand before God our petitions are known in the Word they contemplate; so angels are said to offer our prayers and vows to God, not to teach him but to consult his will about them.
claims: The saints know our petitions in the Word.
Angels offer prayers to consult God's will.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e127.summary: Quotes Augustine: our petitions are made known to the angels with God, so that they offer them to God and consult him, and report to us, openly or secretly, what they learn God commands; so the angel said, 'when you prayed, I offered your prayer to God'.
claims: Angels mediate prayers by consulting God.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e140.summary: Continues Augustine: God's perfection suffices to know all, yet he has messengers, the angels, not to tell him what he does not know, but because it is good for them to consult his truth about their works; they announce what he wills, sent to whom he wills, hearing all in his Word. We too, praying, do not teach him, who knows what we need before we ask, having foreknown from eternity all we would ask and whom he would hear.
claims: Angels consult God's truth, not inform him.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e152.summary: Concludes that an angel is said to offer our prayers to God not as though God did not know what we want, but because rational creatures must refer temporal causes to eternal truth, either asking for themselves or consulting what to do.
claims: Rational creatures refer temporal things to eternal truth.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e158.summary: Argues that if angels learn our petitions from God through his Word and whether to fulfill them, why not believe the saints' souls contemplating God's face understand men's prayers in his truth, and which are to be fulfilled?
claims: Saints know prayers as angels do.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e161.summary: Explains that God is said to hear some prayers not only when he fulfills them but when he makes known to the court of angels and saints what will or will not come of them, and what they know is in God's will they will too, being so devoted to the supreme Truth they can will nothing against his will. So the saints intercede for us by merit, their merits aiding us, and by affection, desiring our wishes fulfilled; yet they do this only (sentence continues).
claims: Saints will only what God wills.
Saints intercede by merit and affection.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e164.summary: Completes: where they have learned it is to be fulfilled in God's will. So we pray that they intercede for us, that their merits aid us and they will our good, since when they will it, God wills it, and so it will be.
claims: We ask the saints to intercede, since their will accords with God's.

pl-l4d45c6-d1e167.summary: Concludes that from the foregoing God deals more mercifully with some than their sins deserve, namely (sentence continues).

pl-l4d45c6-d1e171.summary: Completes: with the moderately bad, who are helped by the Church's suffrages.
claims: God shows mercy to the moderately bad through suffrages.

pl-l4d45c6.summary: Asks whether the saints hear petitions. It is credible that the saints' souls, rejoicing in God's light, understand in contemplating him what happens outside as far as concerns their joy or our help; as angels know our petitions in the Word, so do the saints. Angels offer our prayers to God not to inform him, who knows all eternally, but to consult his will, since rational creatures must refer temporal causes to eternal truth. So the saints know our prayers in God's truth and will only what God wills; they intercede by merit and affection, but only for what they learn God wills; and God deals more mercifully than deserved with the moderately bad helped by the Church's suffrages.
claims: The saints know our petitions in the Word, as angels do.
Angels offer prayers to consult God's will, not to inform him.
Saints intercede by merit and affection, willing only what God wills.
